newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative defects to Liberal Democrats.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative defects to Liberal Democrats.

text.p: A member of Britain's ruling Conservative Party has defected to the opposition Liberal Democrats, but his departure does not affect Prime Minister John Major's tiny parliamentary majority, the Press Association news agency said on Saturday.
Peter Thurnham had already resigned from the party whip, meaning he was not expected to vote with the government.
"I can no longer support a Government which has so lost touch with basic values of decency that they have forfeited the trust and respect of the British people," Thurnam said in a statement.
He was the second Conservative member of parliament to defect to the Liberal Democrats, following Emma Nicholson who quit the ruling party last December.
John Major's parliamentary majority increased to two from just one earlier this week, following the death of an MP from the opposition Labour Party.
Major must call a general election by May next year, with his party lagging Labour by at least 20 points in the most recent opinion polls.
